To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Internet of Things ( IoT ) is subject to law, that there is no technical mechanism to ensure the IoT is lawfully implemented, and that the lack of such mechanism is likely to lead to a situation where the law will be enforced in a manner which is inconsistent with the original intentions of the law makers, leading to a lack of trust in the IoT.

the IoT needs a policy-driven middleware that allows the enforcement of policy, that the audit of policy enforcement is necessary for legal compliance, and that policy-driven middleware must be continuously maintained to allow the IoT to evolve lawfully.

(1) IoT devices must support the enforcement of specified, dynamic policy, such that they align with legal realities; and (2) the enforcement of policy should be audited in order to demonstrate compliance with law and regulation, and to apportion liability.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of policy-driven middleware for IoT applications, systems and networks.
the technical enforcement and audit of policy in the Internet of Things.
the technical mechanisms that enable the enforcement of policy in IoT systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
policy-driven middleware is a necessary component of the Internet of Things.
the Internet of Things (and other systems) must be policy-driven.
policy must be enforced in a way that can be audited, in order for the IoT to be lawful.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
policy-driven middleware for the Internet of Things is a technical mechanism that can be used to enforce legal policy.
the IoT is not just a technical problem but also a legal problem.
we are developing an IoT middleware framework that can enforce legal policies and audit the enforcement of these policies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the IoT requires a policy-driven middleware, that is, a software layer that is able to enforce policy, and that is able to be audited.
the IoT must be built on a policy-driven middleware.
the IoT requires policy-driven middleware that is designed to enforce policy and audit its enforcement, and to support the evolution of both policy and systems.
